pillar_reactions.evidence: Interrupted the presentation with a practical logistics question rather than reacting to the substance — 'Can I interrupt real quick? So do I need to go buy a kettlebell?' — and followed up later with 'Does it matter when you do the exercise?'. Both were answered and he accepted the answers ('Okay.'). Notably he did not connect the mobility content to his own flaring shoulder, and the rep's only reference to it was a generic 'we also want to do five to 10 minutes a day mobility workouts, small protocols, to make sure your shoulders get more freed up'.

Raised a genuine mechanical obstacle to the eating-window concept: 'Yes, but sometimes I do work at night. That does make it kind of a problem.' The rep addressed it directly — 'We've worked with people who work day and night shift sometimes... it's not like we're going to be like, oh, you can only eat between 12 and 6' — and the prospect then accepted fully: 'Oh, absolutely.' A diabetic's nutrition protocol and intermittent fasting were discussed with no reference to his diabetes or his medication schedule by either party.

Agreed without questions or enthusiasm: 'That sounds pretty good.' When the rep pushed for more he could not elaborate and named his own reticence instead — 'I'm really trying not to overthink this... It sounds doable. I want to leave it there.' The rep then supplied the upgrade for him ('let me say it like this. It actually sounds great'), which the prospect went along with. Understood and agreed, but the enthusiasm in the transcript is the rep's rather than the prospect's.

anchors.raw: I'm basically I'm seeing like a little bit of results here but I know like I need structure to get it like myself.
anchors.note: The only product in his head when he hears $6,000 is the gym membership he is already using, which he says is producing visible results — he was no longer getting out of breath sprinting down a hallway and had carried a mattress up a flight of stairs. He never raised this as a price comparison and never disputed the value of the offer, so this is a weak anchor by intent but a real one by economics: $6,000 is a very large multiple of his current spend and he has an unpaid overdraft. Recorded because it is the reference point, not because he argued from it.

unmet_demand.want: To spread the cost over a longer period than the programme allows — 'I want to know how far can I spread this out?'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Third-party financing was stated to require roughly a 600 credit score and the prospect self-reported around 545, which excluded him. The internal plan was capped at six instalments, which the rep priced at $1,200 each. Nothing in the offer reaches a buyer at this level of liquidity.

unmet_demand.want: Training and nutrition that are safe for a diabetic taking multiple daily medications, and that work around a shoulder which flares under pressing
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Never addressed. The prospect disclosed both unprompted and neither he nor the rep returned to them. Intermittent fasting and a progressive loading plan were presented without reference to his condition, and the offer contains no clinical screen or clearance step for the rep to invoke.

unmet_demand.want: A nutrition protocol that works around 7am-to-7pm and rotating night shifts
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Addressed rather than unmet — the rep committed to Trevor building the eating window around his shift pattern. Whether that holds in delivery is untested.
